versions.name: Buffalo Trail Scout Ranch
versions.address: Buffalo Trail Scout Ranch, Fort Davis, TX 79734

features.note: The Outback, a weeklong guided trek on rugged trails.
Latrines with hot showers, commodes, and year-round potable water near the campsites.
Trail to Eagle, the ranch's first-year camper program.
Basketry, leatherwork, pottery, and wood carving.
The Corrals house the ranch's horse herd; riders help feed the horses and clean stalls.
Cavalry and Mountain Man, weeklong immersion treks recreating frontier cavalry and fur-trade life.
The NATECO nature and ecology area.
Troop Night, when units can hike into the outback and stay overnight on the trail.
A small covered pavilion with a picnic table at each campsite.
Open-water diver certification, with dives at Balmorhea State Park.
Free swim, instructional swim, and a mile swim programme.

versions.summary: A 9,000-acre council resident camp set in the Davis Mountains of West Texas.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence). The stored registration page names almost no programme, so codes come from the ranch's own Programs page and from the leader's guide it links; the guide states there are no tent platforms, so platform_tents is deliberately absent.
